transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what brings me in is I keep getting hung up on how my face looks—especially around my jaw. It feels saggy and uneven, like one side of my face looks off. I noticed it a lot after seeing myself in family photos, and now I can’t seem to stop focusing on it, even though my wife and even clients say they barely notice anything.
How much distress would you say these concerns about your face are causing you?

I’m not totally sure how to put a number on it. It bothers me, definitely, but I wouldn’t say it’s completely overwhelming. It’s more like this nagging thing in the back of my mind that makes me feel self-conscious and uncomfortable.
Are you concerned about any other parts of your body besides your face?

Not really, no. It’s mostly my face—specifically that sagging or uneven look around my jaw, like one side looks off. That’s the thing I keep coming back to, especially after seeing those family photos.
Has your concern about your face affected your daily activities or social interactions in any way?

Yeah, somewhat. I still do my job and get through the day, but it slows me down sometimes. Like before client meetings, I can take longer getting ready or hesitating before I leave. And during some appointments I’m not as focused because I’m thinking about how my face looks. Socially, I’ve skipped a few art openings because I didn’t want people looking at me or taking photos.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your face in mirrors or reflections throughout the day?

Yes, I do. Especially before client meetings, I’ll check the bathroom mirror a few times, then sometimes use my phone camera too. I’ll mess with the lighting or change my collar, or try to angle my face differently to see if it looks less uneven. And then once I’m around people, I catch myself comparing my face to younger advisors or people at gallery events instead of just staying in the conversation.
Do you think your face actually looks uneven and saggy, or is it more that you're afraid it might look that way to others?

I think it actually does look that way, at least to me. Like the jaw area looks saggy or uneven, especially one side of my face. It really stood out to me in those family photos, and since then I keep getting stuck on it.

But then my wife says she barely notices anything, and clients don’t seem to react, so… I guess part of me knows it may not be as obvious to other people as it feels to me.
Have you avoided any important life events or opportunities because of your concerns about your face?

Not really major life events, no. I still go to work and handle my clients. But it has affected things some. I’ve been slower getting out the door for client meetings, and during some appointments I’m not as present because I’m thinking about my face. And I’ve skipped a few art openings because I didn’t want to be seen or end up in photos.
Have your concerns about your face changed at all over time, or have they stayed pretty much the same?

It’s gotten more noticeable to me over time, I’d say. It really started sticking in my head after I saw myself in those family photos. Since then I keep focusing on this sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face.

My wife says she barely notices it, and clients don’t seem to either, but I still get stuck on it. It hasn’t really gone away.
Have you noticed any significant impact on your relationships with friends and family due to your concerns about your face?

A little, yeah. I wouldn’t say it’s caused major problems with my family or friends, but I have pulled back from some social things. I’ve skipped a few art openings because I didn’t want people looking at me or taking pictures.

And with work, I still get through it, but I’m slower getting ready for client meetings, and sometimes I’m sitting there not fully present because I’m thinking about how my face looks.
Do you think it would be possible for you to change your perception of your face or do you feel like it's something that is fixed in your mind?

I’d like to think I could change it, but right now it feels pretty fixed in my mind. I keep coming back to that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face, especially since those family photos. Even when my wife or clients don’t seem to notice anything, I still see it.
Do you think you would still be concerned about your face if you were completely alone and nobody could see you?

Yeah, I think I probably would. I mean, it’s worse when I think other people might see it, but even by myself I still get stuck looking at that sagging, uneven part around my jaw and one side of my face. Since those family photos, it’s just kind of been in my head, even though my wife and clients say they barely notice anything.
Is your concern about your face focused on this one specific issue with your jaw and the uneven look, or are there other flaws you're also worried about?

It’s mostly that one thing — the sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. That’s what I keep getting stuck on, especially after seeing those family photos.

I don’t really have a whole list of other flaws I’m focused on. It’s mainly that area, even though my wife and clients say they barely notice it.
Do you feel like you're able to control how often you think about the appearance of your face?

Not really, no. I can try to push it aside, but I keep coming back to that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. It got a lot worse after seeing myself in those family photos. Even when my wife or clients say they barely notice anything, it still sticks in my mind.
Do you think you would be less concerned about your face if everyone around you thought you looked perfect?

Maybe a little, but I don’t think it would completely go away. What brings me in is that I keep getting stuck on that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. Even when my wife and clients say they barely notice anything, I still see it, especially after those family photos.
Do you think you would still think about your face as much if you didn't have to interact with anyone or be seen in public?

Yeah, I think I probably would still think about it. Maybe not as intensely if I wasn’t out seeing people, but it’s not only about other people noticing. I see that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face myself, especially after those family photos, and I get stuck on it even though my wife and clients say they barely notice anything.
Do you think you would still be distressed by your face if you were certain that no one else noticed or cared about its appearance?

Yes, I think I would. Maybe it would take some pressure off if I knew nobody else noticed, but I’d still see it. I keep getting stuck on that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face, especially after seeing it in those family photos. Even when my wife or clients say it’s barely noticeable, it still bothers me.
Do you think your distress about your face is more because of how you think it actually looks or because of how you fear others might see it?

I think it’s more about how I think it actually looks. I do worry what people might see, sure, but what really gets me is I look at my face and keep seeing that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side. It got worse after seeing those family photos. Even when my wife or clients say they barely notice it, I still get stuck on it.
Do you think your distress about your face would decrease if you were certain that your appearance was not being judged by others?

Maybe some, yeah. If I knew for sure nobody was judging it, that would probably ease part of it. But I think I’d still get stuck on it, because I see the sagging and unevenness around my jaw and one side of my face myself. Since those family photos, it’s just been hard not to notice it, even when my wife or clients say they barely see anything.
Do you think your face is actually defective in some way, or is it more that you wish it were perfect?

I don’t know if I’d say it’s actually defective, exactly. It’s more that I keep seeing this sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face, and I get stuck on it. After those family photos, it’s been hard to shake, even though my wife and clients say they barely notice anything.
